document.title: [Bug]: DSpark scheduling using an overly conservative input budget
document.body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Your output of `python collect_env.py` here ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug The scheduler charges each DSpark request `num_new_tokens + K - 1`, where `K` is `num_speculative_tokens`. However, the target/context tokens and the fixed-size draft query block are processed in separate stages. Combining them into one budget can unnecessarily restrict scheduling. For example, assume: ```text max_num_batched_tokens = 16 num_speculative_tokens = 4 2 requests, each scheduling 8 prefill tokens ``` Both requests fit the two stages: ```text target/context stage: 8 + 8 = 16 tokens DSpark query stage: 4 + 4 = 8 tokens ``` Current accounting charges `8 + (4 - 1) = 11` for the first request, so the two requests cannot be admitted in full despite fitting both stages. This may also affect other speculative methods. A possible fix is to keep target and draft-input budgets separate, with each method defining its draft-stage input cost. We may be missing some intended scheduling semantics; we are validating this experimentally and exploring a fix. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
